newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel steady to up, Portuguese tender awarded.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel steady to up, Portuguese tender awarded.

text.p: European fuel markets were slightly firmer on Wednesday as bunker demand boosted barge prices while cargo dealers waited for the results of the Portuguese state utility company's buy tender, traders said.

An Italian trading company was believed to have won the right to supply at least one of the high sulphur fuel cargoes Electricidade de Portugal tendered to buy, while Portuguese refiner Petrogal won a second. It was unclear if EdP took up the option for a third cargo.

The market believed the winning bid was around $8.50 above the mean of NWE fob and Med fob quotes, which was described as aggressive, and traders speculated the Italians would supply the fuel out of tankage.
High sulphur fuel barges traded early at $77.50 fob a tonne and then later jumped to $80/81 in the ARA area.
"When trading first started people didn't realise how much bunker demand there was and they reacted to crude," said one trader. "But swaps were not so bearish and prices picked up."
Low sulphur physical lifted above the swaps numbers to an offer level of around $96 fob, traders said, but buying interest was thin.
One seller was offering 50,000 tonnes via two ports but attracting little interest. One trader was heard looking for material for the eastern Mediterranean.
High freight costs were believed to be discouraging traders from trying to work northern European one percent down to traditional outlets in the Mediterranean.
